messages.body_html:
The Computational Neuroscience lab led by Peter Dayan of the Max Planck
Institute for Biological Cybernetics and the University of Tübingen, in
collaboration with the Neurobiology of Vocal Communication Lab led by
Lena Veit, invites applications for a Postdoc Research Fellow (m/f/d;
E13 TVöD, 100%, 2 years).

This role involves developing statistical and computational models for
characterizing and understanding the structure of animal vocal
communication, starting with the songs of the Bengalese Finch.

This position is suited for researchers who have finished or are about
to finish their PhD in a relevant discipline, such as computational
neuroscience, cognitive (neuro-)science, machine learning, artificial
intelligence, computer science, or psychology. The ideal candidate is
self-motivated, comfortable with both analytic and critical thinking,
and has a strong background in computational neuroscience, machine
learning, or related fields. Relevant areas of expertise include
computational modelling, signal processing, machine learning, and
cognitive modeling. The applicant should have excellent programming
skills, experience with advanced data analysis, and a strong publication
record. The candidate should have a solid knowledge of the literature in
relevant areas, and ideally have experience working in close
collaboration with experimentalists.

The working language is English; command of the German language is not
necessary.

What we offer:

The position, initially limited to 2 years with the possibility of an
extension, is part of a newly established DFG research unit "Neural
Basis of Vocal Communication" (FOR 5768), which investigates, through a
collaborative approach across four research sites, how vocal
communication is produced, coordinated, and learned across vertebrate
species by mapping and comparing the underlying neural networks. Using
behavioral studies, neurophysiological recordings, and computational
modeling, we aim to uncover shared principles and species-specific
adaptations of vocal communication. The position will be supervised by
Peter Dayan and Lena Veit.

We offer remuneration in accordance with TVöD (collective wage agreement
for the Public Service of the German Federal States) in addition to all
the customary benefits granted to employees working in Public
Services. The position is based at the Max Planck Institute for
Biological Cybernetics along with the Werner Reichardt Center for
Integrative Neuroscience which are both in Tübingen.

There are no formal teaching duties, allowing full flexibility for
conducting research. There will be opportunities to mentor and work with
PhD and MSc students working on related topics.

About Tübingen:

Tübingen is a scenic university town on the Neckar River in
South-Western Germany. The quality of life is exceptionally high, and
the atmosphere is diverse, inclusive, and most locals speak
English. Tübingen offers excellent research opportunities due to the
University, three Max Planck institutes, the University Hospital, and
Europe’s largest AI research consortium. You can find out more about
Tübingen here: https://www.tuebingen.de/

How to apply:

If you are interested in the position, please get in touch with Peter
Dayan via email (EMAIL_REDACTED) enclosing your CV. For
formal applications, please send a motivation letter, your CV, up to two
representative publications, and the contact information of two referees
as a single PDF to Susan Fischer (EMAIL_REDACTED). The
MPI for Biological Cybernetics is an equal opportunities
employer. Applications of qualified women academics are especially
encouraged; applications of disabled persons will be given preferential
treatment to those of other candidates with equal qualifications.

Preference will be given to applications received by 28th February 2026, but applications might be considered thereafter until the position is filled.

messages.body_html:
Please circulate the course information among labs/departments/students and social and scientific networks that might be interested. Thank you! 

Brains, Minds and Machines Summer Course 2026 

https://x.com/gkreiman/status/2020962997536162154?s=20 

https://bsky.app/profile/gkreiman.bsky.social/post/3mehd6mgtkk2k 

 

MBL Woods Hole, MA 
Directors: Gabriel Kreiman; Matt Wilson; Boris Katz; Tomaso Poggio 
Location:  MBL, Woods Hole, MA. 
Course Dates: August 7 – August 28, 2026 
Application deadline: March 23, 2026 

Application: Please visit the MBL website to access the application portal: https://www.mbl.edu/education/advanced-research-training-courses/course-offerings/brains-minds-and-machines 

More information:  

https://bmm.mit.edu/ 

 

The basis of intelligence – how the brain produces intelligent behavior and how we may be able to replicate intelligence in machines – is arguably the greatest problem in science and technology. To solve it, we will need to understand how human intelligence emerges from computations in neural circuits, with rigor sufficient to reproduce similar intelligent behavior in machines. Success in this endeavor ultimately will enable us to understand ourselves better, to produce smarter machines, and perhaps even to make ourselves smarter. Today’s AI technologies, such as Watson and Siri, are impressive, but their domain specificity and reliance on vast numbers of labeled examples are obvious limitations; few view this as brain-like or human intelligence. The synergistic combination of cognitive science, neurobiology, engineering, mathematics, and computer science holds the promise to build much more robust and sophisticated algorithms implemented in intelligent machines. The goal of this course is to help produce a community of leaders that is equally knowledgeable in neuroscience, cognitive science, and computer science and will lead the development of true biologically inspired AI. 

 

Invited faculty include Boyden, Brown, DiCarlo, Freiwald, Kaelbing, Katz, Koch, Kreiman, Poggio, Serre, Sompolinsky, Tellex, Tenenbaum, Wilson 

 

Gabriel Kreiman 

CEO, Engramme.com 

Professor, Harvard Medical School 

http://klab.tch.harvard.edu

messages.body_html:
7th International Conference on Mathematics of Neuroscience and AI (Rome, 9-12th June 2026)
-----------------------------------------------------------

We are delighted to announce the 7th International Conference on the Mathematics of Neuroscience and AI, to be held in the Villa Wolkonsky, Rome, Italy, 9-12th June 2026:

www.neuromonster.org

In this exploratory conference we bring together researchers and theorists working on the biological, mathematical, and computational foundations of intelligence across neuroscience, cognitive science, machine learning & artificial intelligence, and related fields.

We hear from leading researchers over four days, spanning neural data, neural theory, cognitive science, and machine learning & artificial intelligence (AI). Each day will have  keynotes, invited speakers, a poster session, and 5 spotlight talks invited from abstract submissions.

Abstract submissions and super-early-bird registration are open (see below).

Keynote Speakers
Professor Tatiana Engel (Princeton)
Professor Gyorgy Buzsaki (NYU)
Professor Noah Goodman (Stanford)
Professor Irina Rish (Montreal & Mila)

Session Chairs
Dr Kris Jensen (UCL)
Jesseba Fernando (Northeastern)
Professor Bill Thompson (Berkeley)
Dr Chen Sun (DeepMind)

Location
The convention will be held at the Villa Wolkonsky, in San Giovanni, Rome (10 minutes walk from the Colosseum).

Submissions
The submission format is an abstract of 250 words, and we invite submissions for each session via the following Google form:

https://forms.gle/dnpQL8HaxiP9snu79

These will be accepted for poster presentation, with the best 5 papers in each session category given an additional spotlight talk. Submission deadline is 28th Feb AOE.

Super-early bird tickets
A limited number of half-price super-early-bird registrations have been posted on our website! Early bird registration will follow.

Come and join the fun!

Dr Ruairidh McLennan Battleday (Thinking About Thinking)
Dr James Whittington (Thinking About Thinking & Oxford)
Dr Giovanni Pezzulo (National Research Council of Italy)
The Organizing Committee.

--
Dr Ruairidh McLennan Battleday BMBCh (Oxon) PhD

President
Thinking About Thinking

messages.title: DUCOG2026 - Submissions now open!
messages.body_html:
Dear All,
 

We are pleased to announce that abstract submission for the XVII. Dubrovnik Conference on Cognitive Science devoted to Adaptations across different timescales is now open! The conference is going to take place on 21-24 May 2026, in the Center for Advanced Studies of Dubrovnik, Croatia, located by the Adriatic sea at the foot of the old city of Dubrovnik, a UNESCO world heritage site.


Adaptation is a defining feature of living systems, from immediate adjustments to long-term developmental and societal changes. Here, we will explore adaptation and its limits across multiple scales, asking how individuals, groups, and societies adjust to shifting internal and external demands, and what this means for personality and mental health. We will be interested in how cognition is adjusted to cope with more immediate challenges like scarcity, threat, or turmoil. On top of that, effects of the environment during sensitive developmental periods can leave enduring marks on information processing and behavioural tendencies. In this vein, we will consider whether cognitive correlates of personality traits and psychopathology can be seen as generalized adaptations to the past, or as obstacles to meeting challenges in the present. In this conference, we will bring together researchers who address this broad question from various angles such as experimental psychology, genetics and neuroscience, or clinical & personality psychology, and use diverse tools such as computational cognitive modelling and time series analysis of daily life data. 


Invited speakers will include:
 

Laura Bringmann (University of Groningen)
Philip Corlett (Yale Unviersity)

Judith R. Homberg (Radboud University)

Stephan Lewandowsky (University of Bristol)
Kevin Mitchell (Trinity College Dublin)


We invite poster submissions from all areas of cognitive science. Both theoretical and empirical posters are welcome.
You may submit your poster abstract here: https://ducog.cecog.eu/submit 


The deadline for abstract submission is 28 February 2026.
Authors will be notified of acceptance of their abstracts by 15 March 2026. 


For more information please visit https://ducog.cecog.eu
or email us at: EMAIL_REDACTED
 
On behalf of the organisers,
Bertalan Polner (Donders Institute & ELTE Eötvös Loránd University) & Levente Rónai (ELTE Eötvös Loránd University & University of Szeged)
- Conference chairs

messages.title: Behavioural Setup Design with Bonsai and Arduino Workshop, March 12-13th 2026
messages.body_html:
Hello!

We are happy to announce our next workshop!

During this workshop, you will learn how to design the behavioural setups that will allow you to answer your research questions most efficiently. Going from theory to practice, we will show you how to plan experiments, make decisions about equipment, reduce confounds, and use an Arduino microcontroller and Bonsai software to build the necessary devices, program the experiments, and collect and analyse behavioural data.

Over two days of intensive, hands-on training, we will show you how to:

  • Plan behavioural experiments in a robust and efficient manner
  • How to avoid bad design decisions
  • Use Arduino to deliver stimuli and control lasers and diodes in optogenetic experiments
  • Control motors and servos to automate elements of your behavioural setups
  • Use sensors with Arduino and record sensor readouts
  • Design and build closed-loop experiments in Bonsai — use behavioural tracking to trigger stimuli, move motors, and much more
  • Choose cameras and data acquisition systems for your experiments
  • Synchronise different data streams and align signals
  • Extract behavioural data and analyse it using Bonsai

No previous experience with programming is necessary!

The workshop will be held at the Nencki Institute in Warsaw on March 12–13, from 10 AM to 6 PM. The workshop fee is PLN 350 (or EUR 85). The application form can be found here  - https://nenckiopenlab.org/design/. The deadline for applications is February 27th.


With best wishes,

NOL Team

messages.author: William Dorrell
messages.title: Cosyne Viewing PArties
messages.body_html:
Dear Systems Neuroscience,

Is there any chance this email could be released?

Best

Will Dorrell

Cosyne Viewing Parties


Cosyne is the preeminent computational neuroscience conference, but a variety of factors limit in-person attendance. Cosyne talks are streamed on youtube, but watching days of talks on your laptop is an agonising way to an aneurism. Cosyne is making videos available online, which offers a third way: regional gatherings that provide partial conference benefits at partial cost. This email provides motivation, and information on how to attend a Cosyne Viewing Party or host your own. For current map of viewing parties see: https://shorturl.at/3DHZX 


Some Motivation: Costs, visa restrictions, and personal responsibilities can make flying round the world to attend a conference impossible. Further, flights contribute around 2.5% of yearly CO2 emissions (and their proportion of warming is even higher, due to contrails and the altitude of emission), but, unlike most other major sources of emissions, there is no feasible green drop-in replacement for flying. This makes reducing flying a key part of almost all realistic net-zero plans.


The Idea: Viewing Parties will run alongside the main conference in Lisbon. They will allow people to gather, capturing some of the advantages of an in-person conference, while making logistics easier and greener. The details are flexible: at its simplest, it can involve hiring a room and screening the talks for an audience who can then discuss what they see. More elaborate versions might draw people from across a large area (e.g. all of South Africa, or the Eastern US) and host poster sessions, social events, or additional discussions alongside talk screenings. This has already worked for ICML, CCN, and NeurIPS.


Host: Hosting can be easy! Simply book a room at your local institution and screen the talks (syncing your screening with the main meeting isn't necessary if time difference is an issue). Additional efforts that might improve the experience include coffee/food, a poster session, organised social events, or additional panel discussions. To register with us and appear on our map (allowing people to find you) email `dorrellwec at gmail.com' with the following information:


  • Where will the Cosyne Viewing Party be hosted?

  • How can people attend?

  • Contact details - who are you?

  • (Optional) Information on the additional events, link to a corresponding webpage, or an invitation to bring posters/talks etc.

messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues,
We are pleased to announce that applications are now open for the 6th edition of the Barcelona Summer School for Advanced Modeling of Behavior (BAMB! 2026).
  • Dates: July 12–23, 2026
  • Location: Barcelona, Spain
  • Application Deadline: 6 March 2026 (midnight Pacific Time)
  • Apply at: www.bambschool.org
BAMB! is an intensive two-week training program for PhD students and early-career researchers in cognitive science, computational neuroscience, and Neuro-AI who possess a strong computational background. For this new edition, we have reformulated the curriculum to address the rapid transformations currently occurring in computational neuroscience, ensuring the course remains at the cutting edge of advanced modeling. The school combines lectures, hands-on tutorials, and group projects to provide both the conceptual foundations and technical skills for the advanced modeling and analysis of behavior. The school is organized by the Centre de Recerca Matemàtica (CRM).
Who should apply: The course is intended for PhD students and postdocs in cognitive, systems, and computational neuroscience with a solid background in computational or quantitative analysis. Proficiency in Python is required. We seek a diverse blend of experimentalists and theoreticians.
A limited number of travel and childcare grants will be available. Scientists from underrepresented groups and countries are especially encouraged to apply.
Topics covered:
  • Modeling fundamentals
  • Decision-making
  • Foraging and sequential decision-making
  • Reinforcement learning
  • Structure learning
  • Complex motor behaviors and time series
Organizers: Alex Hyafil (CRM), Marion Rouault (CNRS, Paris Brain Institute), Heike Stein (CNRS, Sorbonne), Chris Summerfield (Oxford), Klaus Wimmer (CRM), Tarryn Balsdon (CNRS, ENS-PSL), Nisheet Patel (Axy), Manuel Molano-Mazón (UPC), Diksha Gupta (UCL), and Nuria Hernández (CRM).

messages.body_html:
Postdoctoral position in Development and Egocentric Vision.


The Training Program in Integrative Developmental Processes at Indiana University invites applications for a T32-funded postdoctoral fellowship in Bloomington, Indiana. We seek highly motivated individuals interested in research at the intersection of development, vision science, and computer vision. 


The postdoctoral fellow will join a collaborative research environment dedicated to understanding developmental processes through egocentric vision in natural tasks, using advanced computational methods and multimodal datasets to advance developmental theory. Indiana University offers a highly interdisciplinary training environment with exceptional career development and mentoring opportunities. The position will be jointly mentored by Dr. Rowan Candy, whose research integrates behavioral, optical, and neuroscientific approaches to study typical and atypical visual development; and Dr. Kathryn Bonnen, a computational neuroscientist specializing in visuomotor coordination in natural tasks. The broader research community includes faculty from Computer Science (Dr. David Crandall, Dr. Zoran Tiganj), Informatics (Dr. Justin Wood, Dr. Samantha Wood), and Psychological and Brain Sciences (Dr. Linda Smith, Dr. Joshua W. Brown, Dr. Ehren Newman).


Applicants should have strong computational skills and a background in one or more of the following areas: developmental science, vision science, neuroscience, motor control,  computer science, psychology, or related fields.


Eligibility: U.S. citizens or permanent residents who currently hold a doctoral degree or will have met all doctoral program requirements before enrolling.


Applicants should send a cover letter describing their motivation for applying and a curriculum vitae to:

Dr. Rowan Candy (EMAIL_REDACTED)

Dr. Kathryn Bonnen  (EMAIL_REDACTED)

Position is available immediately and will remain open until filled.



--

messages.body_html:
Dear All,
 

We are pleased to announce that abstract submission for the XVII. Dubrovnik Conference on Cognitive Science devoted to Adaptations across different timescales has been extended to 7 March! The conference is going to take place on 21-24 May 2026, in the Center for Advanced Studies of Dubrovnik, Croatia, located by the Adriatic sea at the foot of the old city of Dubrovnik, a UNESCO world heritage site.


Adaptation is a defining feature of living systems, from immediate adjustments to long-term developmental and societal changes. Here, we will explore adaptation and its limits across multiple scales, asking how individuals, groups, and societies adjust to shifting internal and external demands, and what this means for personality and mental health. We will be interested in how cognition is adjusted to cope with more immediate challenges like scarcity, threat, or turmoil. On top of that, effects of the environment during sensitive developmental periods can leave enduring marks on information processing and behavioural tendencies. In this vein, we will consider whether cognitive correlates of personality traits and psychopathology can be seen as generalized adaptations to the past, or as obstacles to meeting challenges in the present. In this conference, we will bring together researchers who address this broad question from various angles such as experimental psychology, genetics and neuroscience, or clinical & personality psychology, and use diverse tools such as computational cognitive modelling and time series analysis of daily life data. 


Invited speakers will include:
 

Laura Bringmann (University of Groningen)
Philip Corlett (Yale Unviersity)

Judith R. Homberg (Radboud University)

Stephan Lewandowsky (University of Bristol)
Kevin Mitchell (Trinity College Dublin)


We invite poster submissions from all areas of cognitive science. Both theoretical and empirical posters are welcome.
You may submit your poster abstract here: https://ducog.cecog.eu/submit 


The deadline for abstract submission is 7 March 2026.
Authors will be notified of acceptance of their abstracts by 15 March 2026. 


For more information please visit https://ducog.cecog.eu
or email us at: EMAIL_REDACTED

messages.body_html:
Dear All,

Dr. Sha’s lab (https://shazhiqiang.wixsite.com/sha-lab) at the University of South Carolina is seeking a full-time Research Assistant (computation focused). Our lab is affiliated with the Carolina Autism & Neurodevelopment Center, the Institute for Mind & Brain, and working closely with the McCausland Center for Brain Imaging in Columbia, the center of SC Metropolitan Statistical Area.

 

Our lab explores the mechanisms of atypical brain development and neurodevelopmental disorders (e.g., autism spectrum disorders) by leveraging computation modeling to bridge neural circuitry, exposure (e.g., early life adversity) and psychopathological phenotypes, and treatment outcomes. These innovative projects will leverage state-of-the-art computational models and deep learning algorithms, supported by the Brain Imaging Center (with 3T and high-field 7T MRI scanners) and the Biobehavioral Research Center.

 

This position provides an excellent opportunity for a motivated student to gain hands-on experience with neuroimaging (e.g., MRI) and computational modeling (e.g., deep learning models), making it ideal preparation for a future graduate or medical career. Research Assistant will be actively involved in the scientific process and are encouraged to contribute meaningfully to publications. We fully support assistants in leading first-author research projects and presenting their work at international conferences.

 

Duties:

·         Computational modeling, construct deep learning models

·         MRI data processing, analysis; present results and publish papers

·         Manage daily administrative operations of the lab (e.g., scheduling and communication)

 

Requirements:

·      Bachelor’s degree in a relevant science (e.g., computational neuroscience, math, data science, engineering, biostatistics, biomedical engineering and etc.)

·         Experience with clinical and MRI data collection and data analysis.

·         Candidates with coding experience are preferred.  

 

How to apply:

Please submit your CV to Dr. Zhiqiang Sha (EMAIL_REDACTED).

messages.body_html:
Tenure-Track Faculty Position

New York University 

Arts & Science (A&S)

Center for Neural Science 

Location: Center for Neural Science

 

Open Date: February 20, 2026


https://apply.interfolio.com/182074

 

Deadline

Review of applications will begin March 31, 2026


Description

The Center for Neural Science (CNS) at New York University (NYU) invites applications for a full-time tenure-track faculty position as an Assistant Professor supported by the Simons Empire Faculty Program. We seek scholars who carry out innovative, rigorous, and impactful research in neuroscience. At the Center for Neural Science, faculty have broad interests in experimental and computational neuroscience as well as neuroengineering and methods-driven approaches, anchored in cognition, perception, and observable behaviors. The Center fosters a collaborative and inclusive environment that privileges excellence, through strong support and mentorship of new faculty, and one of the world’s top doctoral programs in neuroscience. The successful candidate will be expected to lead an internationally-recognized research program that effectively integrates knowledge and techniques across multiple levels of biological organization intended to gain an integrative understanding of cognition and observable behaviors, with a commitment to excellence in teaching and communication. Areas of particular interest include computational neuroscience, neuroengineering. We will only consider candidates doing experimental work that is integral to theory and engineering and do not require any significant wet lab space commitments.


Center faculty are part of a vibrant neuroscience community spanning the Arts and Sciences at the Washington Square campus, the School of Medicine, and the Tandon School of Engineering. The successful applicant will join a collaborative neuroscience community spanning the Arts and Sciences at the Washington Square campus and the Tandon School of Engineering. More information about our department can be found at www.cns.nyu.edu. The appointment can begin as early as September 1, 2026, pending administrative and budgetary approval.


Qualifications

Candidates should have a PhD, MD, or equivalent degree, postdoctoral experience, and a strong record of research achievement. We will only consider candidates who have not yet held a faculty appointment. Appointees will establish their own independent research program, and contribute to the teaching of undergraduate and graduate students, and participate in administrative activities in the Center for Neural Science, the Neuroscience community, and NYU.

 

Application Instructions

Please provide the following materials through Interfolio:

  • Cover letter that includes a brief summary of your most significant research accomplishments.

  • Curriculum vitae.

  • Concise research statement (no more than three pages) that describes (a) your experience and qualifications and (b) your goals and vision for an independent research program, including possible links to the NYU research community.

  • Three recommendation letters, submitted by the referees through Interfolio dossier services. 

  • Copies of at least three representative publications. 

  • Teaching statement (no more than two pages), which includes concrete steps you have taken and that you are planning to take to foster an inclusive intellectual environment for the NYU student population.


For any questions, please contact Jooyeon Kim: EMAIL_REDACTED.

globe. We seek scholars of the highest caliber who are sensitive to the needs of and

possess an interest in working in a broad academic community with different

viewpoints and backgrounds. NYU affirms the value of differing perspectives on the

world as we strive to build the strongest possible university with the widest reach. To

learn more about the Arts & Science commitment to inclusive excellence, please read

here: https://as.nyu.edu/departments/facultyexcellence.html.

messages.body_html:
Dear All,

 

As part of the DFG Cluster of Excellence "The Adaptive Mind" a PhD-student position is available in the Sensorimotor Control and Learning group of the TU Darmstadt (Department of Human Sciences, Institute for Psychology / Centre of Cognitive Science). The position concerns a three-year fixed-term contract and is to be filled from May 1st.

 

In The Adaptive Mind (http://www.theadaptivemind.de), the universities of Giessen, Marburg, and Darmstadt, in collaboration with the University of Frankfurt and the Frankfurt Institute of Advanced Studies (FIAS), pursue the goal of advancing research in the field of Mind, Brain, and Behaviour in an interdisciplinary manner. We combine state-of-the-art behavioral and neurophysiological research with approaches from psychiatry and clinical psychology, as well as quantitative analyses and computational modeling using artificial intelligence, machine learning and robotics. It is the aim of The Adaptive Mind to measure and model the continuous adaptation of natural human behavior in a constantly changing and unpredictable world.

 

The tasks of the available position include scientific research contributions that relate specifically to the purposes of the TAM project, a part of which deals with the Sense of Agency and the neuronal correlates of adaptive perceptual and sensorimotor processes in patients with schizophrenia. Of particular interest are impairments in predictive processes for sensorimotor control. The focus of the position lies in the carrying out and modelling of behavioural experiments with both healthy individuals and, in collaboration with the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy in Marburg, in patient groups.

 

For this purpose we are seeking applications from highly motivated students with an interest in combining theoretical (computational modeling) and experimental research in cognitive science.

 

More information about the position and how to apply, can be found here:

https://www.career.tu-darmstadt.de/tu-darmstadt/job/53070

 

The application deadline is March 7th, 2026. Informal enquiries can be directed to Prof. Loes van Dam (EMAIL_REDACTED).

 

Best Regards,

Loes

Prof. Loes van Dam PhD (she/her)

Sensorimotor Control and Learning
Institut für Psychologie & Centre for Cognitive Science
Technische Universität Darmstadt

messages.author: Nada El Mahmoudi
messages.title: Help shape Open Lab Online – International community survey
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues,
Many of us have faced the same challenge of finding practical and accessible training in open source tools for neuroscience, whether for building behavioural setups, implementing closed loop experiments, classifying behaviour, segmenting imaging data, synchronizing devices, or analysing complex datasets.
We believe these skills should be easier to access and shared more openly across institutions.
Building on the initiative and experience of the Nencki Open Lab (https://nenckiopenlab.org/), we are launching Open Lab Online, a new international and community driven series of online, hands on workshops dedicated to open-source tools for neuroscience, including behaviour, experimental control, synchronization, and data analysis.
Our goal is to extend the Open Lab spirit internationally through accessible online training and the exchange of expertise across labs and countries.
To make this initiative truly useful, we need your input. Please take 5 to 10 minutes to complete the short survey below and let us know which tools, skills, and topics would be most valuable to you:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd1dJxECfbr6geQMt9BtSpSPslq-zlHnd6oW2OH1wg02ruTEQ/viewform?usp=header
Your responses will directly influence the content and format of the upcoming workshops.
If this resonates with you, please feel free to share the survey within your networks.
Let’s build a more open, practical, and technically empowered neuroscience community together.
Best regards,
Nada El Mahmoudi & Mateusz Kostecki
Open Lab Online Initiative


Dr. Nada El Mahmoudi

topics.snippet: Dear Systems Neuroscience community: The Grossman Center for Quantitative Biology and Human Behavior

messages.author: Jorge Jaramillo
messages.title: Postdoctoral fellows in computational neuroscience at the University of Chicago
messages.body_html:
Dear Systems Neuroscience community: 

The Grossman Center for Quantitative Biology and Human Behavior at the University of Chicago seeks outstanding applicants for multiple postdoctoral positions in computational and theoretical neuroscience. We especially welcome applicants who develop mathematical approaches, computational models and/or data analysis methods to study the brain at the circuits, systems, or cognitive levels. The Grossman Center faculty members to work with are: (informal enquiries are welcome)

  • Brent Doiron’s lab investigates how the cellular and synaptic circuitry of neuronal circuits supports the complex dynamics and computations that are routinely observed in the brain. (EMAIL_REDACTED). 
     
  • Stephanie Palmer’s lab studies how the behavioral goals of an organism shape how it senses the world, using a variety of tools from information theory and statistical physics. (EMAIL_REDACTED). 
  • Jorge Jaramillo’s lab investigates multiareal brain circuits underlying cognitive processes such as memory, attention, and decision making through dynamical systems modeling. (EMAIL_REDACTED). 
  • Ramon Nogueira’s lab investigates the geometry of representations as the computational support of cognitive processes like abstraction in noisy artificial and biological neural networks. (EMAIL_REDACTED). 
  • Marcella Noorman’s lab studies how biological constraints shape the neural circuit dynamics that enable flexible, efficient computations necessary for cognitive functions like navigation. (EMAIL_REDACTED).
  • Samuel Muscinelli’s lab studies how brain circuit anatomy shapes learning and adapts to it. We combine modeling, machine learning, and data analysis with experimental collaborators. (EMAIL_REDACTED)

Appointees will have access to state-of-the-art facilities and multiple opportunities for collaboration with exceptional experimental labs within the Neuroscience Institute, as well as other labs from the departments of Physics, Computer Sciences, and Statistics.

The Grossman Center offers competitive postdoctoral salaries in the vibrant and international city of Chicago, and a rich intellectual environment that includes the Argonne National Laboratory, Chicago’s National Institute for Theoretical and Mathematical Biology (NITMB), and UChicago’s Data Science Institute and Center for Living Systems. The Neuroscience Institute at UChicago is currently engaged in a major expansion that includes the incorporation of several new faculty members in the next few years. 

APPLICATIONS:

Please send your application before April 4th, 2026, as a single PDF file to EMAIL_REDACTED. It must include:

  1. CV with publications highlighted;
  2. A motivation letter specifying the types of projects you would like to work on;
  3. The names and contact details of two academic references.

Earliest start date: June 1st, 2026, or via mutual agreement.

messages.author: Jorge Mejias
messages.title: Applications open for the Computational & Cognitive Neuroscience Summer School in Suzhou, China
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues,

We would like to let you know that the application period for the CSHA Computational and Cognitive Neuroscience Summer School are now open. If you know of any PhD students or early postdocs (in your own labs or elsewhere) interested in learning cutting edge computational neuroscience topics during three weeks in July in beautiful Suzhou, China, please let them know about this opportunity. The deadline for applications is April 1st: https://ccnss.net/ 

Our faculty list for this year includes top computational neuroscience researchers like Gustavo Deco, Rainer Goebel, Tatiana Engel, Naoshige Uchina, Cristina Savin, Xiao-Jing Wang, and many others. Students will also work on individual projects guided by experienced TAs (senior postdocs from top labs) and aided by the school’s faculty.

On top of all the science, attending the school will give all participants the chance to explore China and the Shanghai region. Citizens from multiple countries (including many Europeans) don’t need a visa to travel and stay in China for up to 30 days (which covers the whole duration of the school). It’s truly a golden opportunity :)

Thank you very much in advance for your help in spreading this news!


Best wishes,

 

Jorge Mejias

 

On behalf of the organizing committee:

Xiao-Jing Wang (New York University)

Áine Byrne (University of College Dublin)

Chengcheng Huang (University of Pittsburgh)

Songting Li (Shanghai Jiao Tong University)

Hello,

I’m reaching out to share an opportunity that may be of interest to you and your network. Applications for the 2026 Neuromatch Academy courses are now open until 15 March. 

Neuromatch runs intensive, live, online courses built around small learning groups called pods, where participants learn collaboratively with peers and a dedicated Teaching Assistant while working on a mentored group project. Pods are matched by time zone, research interests, and, when possible, language preference.

The 2026 live course options are:
6–24 July: 
Computational Neuroscience
Deep Learning
13–24 July: 
NeuroAI
Computational Tools for Climate Science

They are great for advanced undergraduates, MSc or PhD students, post baccalaureates, research staff, and early career researchers. The courses are designed for anyone preparing for research that intersects neuroscience, machine learning, data science, and modeling, and for those who want structured, collaborative learning combined with a hands-on research project in a global cohort.

There is no cost to apply. 
Tuition is adjusted by local cost of living and tuition waivers are available during enrollment for those who need them.

Course details, dates, and FAQs: https://neuromatch.io/courses/

messages.author: Ruidong Chen
messages.title: Neurobiology of Cognition 2026
messages.body_html:
Hi all,

Please consider submitting an abstract to the 2026 Neurobiology of Cognition Gordon Research Seminar (GRS), taking place July 18-19, 2026 at Waterville Valley, New Hampshire.

The GRS is a unique trainee-only (graduate students and post-docs) opportunity for early-career scientists to share their research and build a supportive community of peers exploring the neural basis of cognition. This year’s theme, “Cells, Circuits, and Computation,” focuses on bringing together diverse approaches to understanding cognitive function. We are especially interested in work that employs computational modelling, theoretical analysis, or Machine Learning inspired frameworks to understand cognitive functions. The GRS will feature two poster sessions where all attendees can present a poster. Attendees can also apply for a short talk. For full consideration, applicants interested in giving a talk should apply before April 12th.

In addition to the scientific program, the GRS will have many opportunities for informal networking and career-focused discussions.

We highly encourage trainees to also apply for the associated Gordon Research Conference (GRC) that follows (July 19-24). Please share this opportunity within your labs and networks!

Here are the links to apply:

GRS

GRC



Best,
Ruidong Chen

messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues and friends,

 

[Please accept our apologies if you get multiple copies of this message]

You can now register to SBDM 2026 (27-29 May, Paris, France), from now to May 22nd.

You can also submit abstracts for poster presentation, from now to March 27th.

Notifications of acceptance for the abstracts will be sent on March 31st.

 

Both registration and submission can be made on our website: https://sbdm2026.sciencesconf.org/

Please circulate widely and encourage your colleagues and team members to attend.

 

Best regards,

SBDM organisers.

 

NB: SBDM 2026 is the 13th Symposium on Biology of Decision Making. 

This year we will have two days organized at the Paris Brain Institute (Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital) and one day at the NeuroModulation Institute (Sainte-Anne Hospital). 

The aim is to bring together the various fields interested in how brains make decisions (neuroscience, philosophy, economics, cognition, robotics, psychiatry, ethology, etc.)
